Title: Disappointing change to 1D Change
Review:
The recent decision to restrict the 1D Change feature to shares held through INDmoney is a bad move.

One of the key advantages of INDmoney was being able to track your overall portfolio across different brokers. If I have investments with multiple brokers, I should still be able to use INDmoney to see the combined 1D movement of my holdings.

Restricting this feature to INDmoney holdings makes the app considerably less useful as a portfolio tracking tool and feels more like an attempt to encourage users to move their investments onto the platform.

Some users may have chosen INDmoney specifically because it worked across brokers. Changes like this can fundamentally change how those users use the app.

Please reconsider and bring back cross-broker 1D Change tracking.

Title: Discrepancy in adding money to the wallet
Review:
I have a serious Concern regarding USD/INR exchange rate and transparency of charges

I am disappointed with the way USD deposits are being processed through INDmoney/Federal Bank. I recently tried to deposit ₹50,000 into my US wallet, and the app showed an exchange rate of ₹96.25/USD, while the prevailing USD/INR rate at the time was around ₹94.26/USD.

This represents a difference of approximately ₹1.99 per USD, or 2.1%, which is significant for a currency conversion. For a ₹50,000 transaction, this exchange-rate difference alone can materially reduce the USD amount received.

The app also displayed ₹74.89 GST and ₹8,321 indicative TCS. I understand that TCS is refundable and therefore should not necessarily be considered a permanent cost. However, the exchange-rate spread is a separate issue and needs much greater transparency.

My concern is not simply about paying a fee — it is about fair and transparent valuation of the money being converted. If Federal Bank/INDmoney is applying a currency-conversion markup, customers should clearly be shown the reference USD/INR rate, the markup/spread being applied, and the exact amount being charged because of that spread.

The statement “You’re saving ₹1,796 on transfer charges and forex rates” also creates the impression that the conversion is highly competitive, while the displayed exchange rate appears materially higher than the prevailing market rate.

I request INDmoney to clearly disclose how this exchange rate is determined and what portion of the difference represents the bank’s forex spread. Customers should be able to see a transparent calculation before approving the transaction.

Please improve the transparency of USD/INR conversion rates and ensure customers receive a fair and properly evaluated exchange rate.

Title: Disappointed with the UPI device restriction
Review:
I was genuinely surprised to see that INDmoney has discontinued UPI functionality on iPhone 12 and below and requires an iPhone 13 or newer.

My iPhone 11 is still running a supported/current iOS version and works perfectly well with other UPI and financial apps. If this is a security decision, the requirement should ideally be based on the supported iOS/security version rather than an arbitrary iPhone model.

Other platforms such as Groww continue to support UPI on iPhone 11. Because of this restriction, I am now considering moving my IPO and investment activities to another platform.

Unfortunately, with this decision, INDmoney may have lost two customers — mine and my wife’s.

I hope INDmoney reconsiders this policy and provides support for iPhone 11 rather than forcing customers to change their devices or platforms.

Even if banking or exchange-rate processing is involved, the app should clearly mention this upfront and improve the wallet funding process. This delay can make users miss investment opportunities.

My first experience with INDmoney has been very disappointing. Please don’t just ask users to email some support address. Take this feedback seriously, fix the issue, and improve the platform.
